scenario.name: Kaspersky GReAT — ToddyCat APT: ESET Scanner DLL Proxying (CVE-2024-11859) & TCESB Loader
scenario.shortSubtitle: Kaspersky Securelist · Signed ESET ecls.exe, version.dll Search-Order Hijack & TCESB In-Memory Implant
scenario.overview: Imagine a modern glass office building where visitors check in with the front-desk receptionist, scan a badge at the lobby turnstile, and walk between glass-walled meeting rooms. In the sunlit office building lobby, an unbadged visitor talks past the front-desk receptionist and persuades the desk clerk to print a temporary building pass. In this real-world scenario, the intruder steps up to the lobby badge turnstile blending in with everyday guests, then quietly copies a trusted access pass from the front-desk receptionist's station. When building security compares the receptionist sign-in sheet against the turnstile badge swipes across the glass offices, the unescorted hallway trail is exposed. In this scenario (CVE-2024-11859, Kaspersky GReAT, ToddyCat APT: ESET Scanner DLL Proxying (CVE-2024-11859) & TCESB Loader) on WKS-19 (10.10.30), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: launching the Signed ESET Scanner Alongside, then proxying Legitimate DLL Exports While, then establishing an Encrypted C2 Channel. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Launching the Signed ESET Scanner Alongside, then Proxying Legitimate DLL Exports While, then Establishing an Encrypted C2 Channel, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 7 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: ESET ECLS.EXE VERSION.DLL HIJACK (CVE-2024-11859)
stages.subtitle: Signed ecls.exe loads malicious version.dll from current directory
stages.description: In the sunlit office building lobby, an unbadged visitor talks past the front-desk receptionist and persuades the desk clerk to print a temporary building pass. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder steps up to the lobby badge turnstile blending in with everyday guests while everyday visitors and the front-desk receptionist go about their routine. On workstation GOV-WKS-19 (10.10.30.18), the attacker drops a standalone, validly signed copy of ESET Command Line Scanner (ecls.exe, an authentic antivirus utility whose valid digital signature passes Windows AppLocker and antivirus file checks) into a writable folder like C:\ProgramData\ESET\ right next to a malicious library named version.dll. Because of CVE-2024-11859 (where ecls.exe did not restrict its DLL load path to System32), the moment ecls.exe starts, Windows loads the attacker’s version.dll from C:\ProgramData\ESET\ before checking C:\Windows\System32\version.dll. Unlike KnownDLLs (such as kernel32.dll or ntdll.dll, which Windows forces every program to load exclusively from System32), version.dll is not on the Default KnownDLLs list, so any executable that imports version.dll without specifying LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_SYSTEM32 will load a local version.dll from its own folder first. Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ HIJACK VERSION.DLL / ⇠#1 ACK CVE-2024-11859) from Node ① (#1 ToddyCat C2 Server) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Kaspersky Anti-Targeted Attack).

stages.title: TCESB IN-MEMORY DECRYPTION & EDR EVASION
stages.subtitle: Decrypting TCESB shellcode inside ecls.exe trusted process space
stages.description: Instead of staying in the public waiting chairs, the visitor taps that pass at the lobby turnstile and walks down the hallway from one glass meeting room to the next. Here in Step 2 inside the office building, the intruder uses borrowed access inside the office building to slip closer to the executive glass meeting room without disturbing the public lobby waiting area. If the attacker’s version.dll failed to answer the normal version-check functions that ecls.exe calls on startup (like GetFileVersionInfoW), ecls.exe would crash immediately with an error popup. To prevent a crash, the malicious version.dll uses DLL Export Proxying (forwarding every normal API call straight through to the real C:\Windows\System32\version.dll so ecls.exe runs smoothly), while its background thread reads an encrypted file from disk and decrypts ToddyCat’s TCESB backdoor directly into RAM. By adding linker export forwarders in the malicious DLL’s Export Address Table (pointing functions like GetFileVersionInfoW to C:\Windows\System32\version.GetFileVersionInfoW), the host program continues to work normally while the attacker’s decrypted shellcode runs in the same process memory. Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ TCESB UNPACK RAM / ⇠#2 ALERT 184 KB RWX) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 ecls.exe (Signed ESET Scanner)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Kaspersky Anti-Targeted Attack).

stages.title: DPAPI COOKIE THEFT & HTTPS C2 EXFILTRATION
stages.subtitle: Harvesting Chrome/Edge session cookies and beaconing to ToddyCat C2
stages.description: Inside the executive glass conference room, the intruder opens the unlocked cabinet and copies private project folders while staff walk by outside thinking they belong there. In this final step inside the office building, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the front-desk receptionist's station until the reception sign-in logbook catches the mismatch. Running inside the memory space of the signed ecls.exe process (so process lists show a legitimate ESET security scanner), the decrypted TCESB backdoor opens an encrypted HTTPS tunnel on TCP port 443 to ToddyCat command-and-control server 203.0.113.142:443 to harvest domain credentials and browser cookies. Quoting the story beat above, that physical action maps onto [object Object] and [object Object] (the exact host or protocol control point this stage must exercise before the next kill-chain move can start). Why is this still detectable by defenders? Because ecls.exe is a standalone, offline on-demand file scanner that never connects to the internet during normal operation, meaning any Sysmon EventID 3 (NetworkConnect) log showing ecls.exe opening an outbound TCP/443 socket is an immediate indicator of compromise. In the documented Sysmon EID 3 exchange from ecls.exe (Signed ESET Scanner) to version.dll Proxy & TCESB RAM, version.dll Proxy & TCESB RAM responds with ACK TLS 1.3 (confirming that the ECLS.EXE C2 BEACON request succeeded on version.dll Proxy & TCESB RAM and completing the final execution objective of Kaspersky GReAT, ToddyCat APT: ESET Scanner DLL Proxying (CVE-2024-11859) & TCESB Loader). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ ECLS.EXE C2 BEACON / ⇠#3 ACK TLS 1.3) from Node ③ (#3 ecls.exe (Signed ESET Scanner)) to Node ④ (#4 version.dll Proxy & TCESB RAM), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Kaspersky Anti-Targeted Attack).

detectionRule.title: Kaspersky GReAT — ToddyCat ESET ecls.exe version.dll Hijack (CVE-2024-11859)
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: System DLL version.dll Loaded from Non-System32 Path (CVE-2024-11859)
logsource:
  category: image_load
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ImageLoaded|endswith: '\version.dll'
  filter_system32:
    ImageLoaded|startswith:
      - 'C:\Windows\System32\'
      - 'C:\Windows\SysWOW64\'
      - 'C:\Windows\WinSxS\'
  condition: selection and not filter_system32
level: high
detectionRule.mitigation: Hunt for any process loading version.dll, winhttp.dll, or dbghelp.dll from outside C:\Windows\System32\ and update ESET tools past CVE-2024-11859.

detectionRule.title: Kaspersky GReAT — ToddyCat TCESB version.dll Proxy Loader
detectionRule.ruleCode:
rule Kaspersky_APT_ToddyCat_TCESB_ProxyDLL {
  meta:
    author = "Kaspersky GReAT"
    cve = "CVE-2024-11859"
  strings:
    $s1 = "GetFileVersionInfoSizeW" ascii
    $s2 = "VerQueryValueW" ascii
    $s3 = "\\System32\\version.dll" wide ascii nocase
  condition:
    uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and all of them
}
detectionRule.mitigation: Block execution of standalone AV command-line scanners from user-writable directories via AppLocker / WDAC.

detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Suspicious Outbound Connection by ESET ecls.exe (ToddyCat)
